items.finding: The temperature sensitivity of the OH bands is a severe drawback for measuring aqueous solution in NIR and MIR, which makes tempered sample holders necessary.
items.how_it_applies: Since temperature variations affect aqueous bands in MIR and NIR, monitoring process temperature concurrently at the measurement point should be tested to correct for spectral shifts.
items.limits_and_transfer_risks: The cited study addresses general spectral characteristics rather than the specific customer matrix or instrument, so temperature compensation models must be validated on the customer's actual process fluid.

citation.quote: Additionally, the temperature sensitivity of the OH bands is a severe drawback for measuring aqueous solution in NIR and MIR, which makes tempered sample holders necessary [29].
citation.label: E01 ¶12

items.finding: Instrument complementarity was not always sufficient to improve the predictive performance of several critical quality attributes when fusing Raman and FT-IR data.
items.how_it_applies: When combining methods such as MIR ATR and Raman, one must verify that the fused model actually outperforms single-method models on held-out batches before committing to multi-method integration.
items.limits_and_transfer_risks: The cited finding stems from a specific food analytical study combining Raman and FT-IR, which may not translate to the customer's specific chemical system or liquid matrix.

citation.quote: In some situations, instrument complementarity (not data complementarity) was not sufficient to improve the performance of predictive several CQAs, as shown by a Raman and FT-IR data based food analytical study [73].
citation.label: E02 ¶36
